text:
alex: quick update — i pushed a staging dashboard that shows hotpath token cost + live cache-savings attribution per-route. preview: https://staging.redwood.internal/dash/hotpath-cost :eyes:

jamie: nice. what's the sampling rate on that? we need to know how noisy the savings numbers will be.

alex: default sampling is 1% for full traces, fallback to aggregated counts for the rest. query looks like:
```sql
select route, sum(tokens) as toks, sum(cost) as gross_cost, sum(cache_saved_tokens) as saved
from hotpath_events_sampled
group by route
```

maria: is the "saved" column already crediting shared prefetch? last time that bit caused big argument.

alex: good call — right now saved = direct KV hits only. shared prefetch crediting is off; i wanted to discuss policy before wiring it in.

ryan: +1 to discussing. our choices: 1) naive per-route credit (fast, but double-counts shared prefetch), 2) amortize across routes that touch the prefetch key within window, 3) tenant-level bucket and admin manual adjustments.

jamie: UX perspective: if we show amortized credits, we need to surface the heuristic and a confidence score. otherwise PMs will assume it's exact. maybe a little info icon with math and sample rate.

alex: agree. proposal: show two columns — `raw_kv_hits` and `amortized_kv_credit` + `confidence`. default display raw, toggle to amortized.

maria: how expensive will computing amortized credits be? could blow up in the query engine.

alex: implemented amortization offline via a nightly job for now. staging shows near-realtime by using a 10m window micro-batch. costs are bounded but we need to tune retention for heavy tenants.

ops-bot: deploy 6598881234-hotpath-cost -> staging succeeded in 18s

ryan: regarding per-model economics: do we map to model sku or to underlying variant? customers ask for per-model because quantization affects cost-per-token.

alex: current mapping is to model SKU (e.g., gpt-3.8q, redwood-1.2). we also have a `variant` tag for quantization level. dashboard can pivot on either.

jamie: small UI ask: can we add a tiny sparkline for token variance over the last hour per-route row? helps spot noisy routes.

alex: yup — added a sparkline column in staging.

maria: rollout plan? i don't want this in prod until QA sanity-checks the amortization numbers. we should also hide the amortized column behind a feature flag.

alex: agreed. flag is `hotpath_cost_amortized`. turning off by default in prod. i'll add an explicit tooltip that calls out sampling and nightly vs micro-batch sources.

ryan: one more: make sure the API that powers the dashboard exposes provenance so infra can pull raw signals for billing reconciliation. a small protobuf or JSON blob with `source: ["sampled", "aggregated", "amortized_job"]` and `sample_rate` would help.

alex: noted — API will include `provenance` field. example record attached in the staging endpoint.

jamie: can we add a tiny CTA to export per-route CSV for a date range? PMs will ask to drop into sheets.

alex: export button added (staging). CSV contains `provenance` per row.

maria: ok let's schedule a quick 20m review tomorrow to validate numbers before we flip the flag. i'll invite finance + product.

ryan: thanks — and alex, please add a short runbook for interpreting negative "amortized_kv_credit" values (they happen when eviction + prefetch overlap).

alex: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
